_note: Manager dossiers — day jobs, schools, cities and verified company facts, kept as raw material for roasts, toasts and burn generation. Nothing here is rendered on the site by default; it is the reference file. Sources: manager-supplied LinkedIn profiles plus public reporting on the companies (linked in company_facts).

andrew.name: Andrew
notes: Has run this league for years. Won it for the first time in 2025, which means the champion and the person who certifies the champion are the same man.
Renamed the franchise from Hail Mary to Hail Purdy mid-title-run.
2025 auction: biggest buy $36 Ladd McConkey, nothing over $40, and a ring.
andrew.tenure: Commissioner for the better part of a decade
company_facts: Coinbase is the largest US crypto exchange; its app is famous for going down at exactly the moment everybody needs it.
Its 2022 Super Bowl ad was a bouncing QR code with no words, and the resulting traffic crashed the app.
roast_angles: Works in crypto and won this league by refusing to buy anything expensive. He has watched enough people go all-in at the top to know exactly what it looks like.
Commissioner, champion, and the man who investigates the commissioner. Three roles, one guy, zero recusals.
His draft board is the single most boring document this league has produced, and it beat everybody.

abhishek.name: Abhishek Purohit
notes: Built this website. Which means he built a permanent public monument to his own second-place finish.
Burned his entire $1,000 FAAB budget to $0 in 2025.

barrett.name: Barrett Davis
barrett.title: CEO
barrett.school: University of Georgia (Terry College of Business)
company_facts: NterNow is Atlanta proptech: self-guided home tours — ID scan, background check, 2FA, then a single-use code opens a smart lock and a stranger wanders an empty house alone.
Claims builders capture 3–5x more leads; ~25% of its million-plus tours happen outside 10am–6pm.
Acquired by Allegion, the parent company of Schlage.
roast_angles: Built a business on letting strangers into empty houses at 2am with no supervision — the same energy as his waiver wire.
The company's whole value proposition is that no human needs to show up. He extended that philosophy to setting his lineup.
Got bought by a lock company. Fitting: his playoff hopes have been locked out before.

neil.name: Neil
notes: The team is called Shut Up because it is the single most common thing said to him in this league. It has never worked.
Left after 2025. Most points in the league (1,941.94), tied-best record at 22-6, finished third.
roast_angles: Named his team after the thing everyone says to him and then kept talking for another decade.
A dentist: aggressive verbally, conservative with the drill. Scored more than anyone and left with the most money and no ring.
The first recorded case of a dentist getting drilled.

mohsin.name: Mohsin
notes: Left after 2025. Team was named Bullish; also ran Bearish. Both bore the same result.
Owns the most Saccos in league history — 2016, 2018 and 2022, all three lost in the bowl.

nishil.name: Nishil Naik
nishil.title: Business Development Manager
company_facts: Marben is a 30+ year old embedded communications software company: protocol stacks and toolkits sold to equipment makers.
Product list includes V2X (vehicle-to-everything road safety), ASN.1 compilers, Diameter signaling for 4G/LTE/IMS, and — still, in 2026 — legacy OSI protocol stacks.
Customers include Bosch, Cisco, Ericsson, Nokia, Renault.
roast_angles: His job is selling ASN.1 compilers and Diameter signaling stacks, a sentence that has ended every conversation he has ever started at a party.
Sells technology that lets cars talk to each other to avoid collisions, and cannot avoid a bye-week collision on his own roster.
Works for a company still shipping OSI — a networking standard that lost to TCP/IP forty years ago. Perfect employer for a man still starting a guy who retired.
Took the Sacco in back-to-back years, 2013 and 2014. Business development.

maclane.name: Maclane Matsuoka
maclane.title: Strategic IT
company_facts: Pellera was created in April 2025 when H.I.G. Capital took Converge Technology Solutions private and merged it with Mainline Information Systems.
The name is invented. Two real companies went in; one made-up word came out.
roast_angles: Works for a company whose name was generated the way you generate a fantasy team name: take two real words, delete the meaning, add a vowel.
Converge plus Mainline equals Pellera. That is the same math that produced his starting lineup.
Three business cards in eighteen months and still one ring.

darrius.name: Darrius Marzette
darrius.title: Senior Claims Adjuster
company_facts: Assurant is a Fortune 500 specialty insurer, ~$12B revenue: phone protection plans, extended warranties, lender-placed home insurance, vehicle service contracts.
Certus is a separate claims administrator — treat them as two employers, not one company.
A senior claims adjuster is the person professionally responsible for finding the reason your claim is denied.
roast_angles: Denies claims for a living, which is exactly how he processed his own season: submitted with confidence, reviewed, rejected on a technicality.
Spends all day telling people 'that's considered normal wear and tear' and still couldn't tell his own roster was totaled.
Works in the extended-warranty industrial complex: profits off other people's bad decisions, and still couldn't spot a bust in round two.

greg-miley.name: Greg Gokey
greg-miley.title: Regional Director, Southeast District — Technology Solutions Provider market
greg-miley.school: University of Georgia (Terry College of Business)
company_facts: The Redesign Group is a fast-growing technology and cybersecurity channel partner: 1,900+ customers, ~345% three-year growth, #9 on CRN's 2026 Fast Growth 150.
Vendor badges include Dell Titanium Black, Dell North American Data Center Partner of the Year 2026, Broadcom Pinnacle Partner, Rapid7 Emerging Partner of the Year.
Its notable 2026 news was redesigning its own logo.
roast_angles: Played poker for a living and then lost the 2025 Sacco Bowl to a 4-24 team that had stopped opening the app. 180.90 to 234.22. He has calculated worse odds and still landed on the wrong side.
More trophies for reselling other people's servers than for anything he has done here — and he has a ring, which somehow makes it worse.
Works at a company called REDESIGN and could not redesign a lineup that lost by 53 points to a man who wasn't trying.

greg-ir.name: Greg Gagne
greg-ir.title: Director
company_facts: Truist was formed in December 2019 by the ~$66B BB&T/SunTrust merger; ~$500B in assets, ~1,900 branches.
The name was produced by a branding firm and mocked on the day it was announced; Truliant Federal Credit Union sued over it.
They then paid to rename SunTrust Park, so the Braves play in a stadium named after a word that does not exist.
roast_angles: Works at a bank whose name was invented by consultants, hated on arrival, and immediately sued over — which is also the best description of his lineup: technically almost a real thing.
A Director at Truist: important enough to be in the meeting, not important enough to end it.
The one Auburn man in a room full of Georgia degrees, and he still isn't the most embarrassed person here.

anuj.name: Anuj
company_facts: Express-tunnel car washes: 40%+ store-level EBITDA margins, 70–80% gross margins, ~3-year payback.
The engine is the unlimited monthly membership — at Mister Car Wash subscriptions went from 45% of sales in 2020 to 74% by 2024, with members averaging only 2–4 washes a month.
Private equity overbuilt it: ZIPS Car Wash filed Chapter 11 in early 2025 to shed ~$279M of debt; Mister Car Wash trades roughly 50% below its IPO price.
roast_angles: Owns an industry whose entire profit model is people paying monthly for something they forget to use — which is also his relationship with his fantasy team.
Private equity looked at soap and water and invented a SaaS company. He looked at a running back committee and invented a losing season.
Saved himself from the 2025 Sacco by outscoring Greg by 34 points in one week. The only clean escape in the file.

nathan.name: Nathan
company_facts: US off-premise liquor retail: 36,000+ stores, ~$51B in sales, net margins of only ~3–9% after rent, labor, licensing and shrink.
Beer drives traffic on the thinnest spread; spirits carry the best gross margin.
'Recession-proof' is such a tired claim that the industry's own trade press publishes articles debunking it — and the actual threat is sober-curious and GLP-1, not a recession.
roast_angles: Sells liquor on the theory that it's recession-proof, a claim so tired that his own industry writes debunking articles about it.
3–9% net margins on booze means he makes more money when his customers make worse decisions, which makes this league his single most profitable account.
The one variable no model priced in: people voluntarily not drinking. The other: him voluntarily not setting a lineup.

will.name: Will
notes: Nobody in this league can say what Will does for a living. The job title is still classified.
Team has been Good Will Hunting long enough that the movie joke has aged into a mystery.

jon-gragg.name: Jonathan Gragg
jon-gragg.title: Leads analytics for FanDuel Canada
jon-gragg.experience: 10+ years; leads analytics across CRM, marketing, VIP and commercial for sportsbook and casino
company_facts: FanDuel is the largest US sportsbook — roughly 44% of gross gaming revenue, ~$5.3B revenue in 2025, owned by Flutter Entertainment.
FanDuel Canada operates only in Ontario, the one province with a legal open iGaming market.

In January 2026 Ontario's AGCO fined FanDuel CAD $350,000 for accepting 144 bets on Czech table-tennis matches loaded with match-fixing red flags, including bettors winning at a near-perfect rate, and failing to flag it.
Fined $125K by Iowa regulators in July 2025.
roast_angles: Spent a decade getting paid to study degenerate behavior and then voluntarily moved into the enclosure. He does not need to ask how your season is going. He can see it.
Knows which one of us takes the Thursday parlay at 11:40pm, and has known for years.
The first man in league history who can model his own tilt in advance and will do it anyway.

tom-alshouse.name: Tom Alshouse
tom-alshouse.title: Regional Sales Manager
company_facts: Family-owned craft cidery and distillery on Marietta Square, founded by Mark and Liz Deno after home-brewing in their garage.
Bills itself as Georgia's top-selling craft cider; also makes vodka, gin, eau de vie, apple brandy and hemp seltzers.
Taproom is open four days a week. The events calendar is drag bingo, trivia, yoga and line dancing.
roast_angles: Sells a beverage with no natural enemies, because nothing has ever chosen it. Cider is what you order when the bar is out and you aren't brave enough to say you don't like beer.
Fourteen men who scream about running backs now have a dedicated apple juice supplier.
The league has never been more hydrated or less intimidating.
